articles.title: Apple is giving iPhone 14 and 15 users another free year of satellite features
articles.summary: iPhone 14 and iPhone 15 users are getting an additional year of free access to satellite connectivity features, according to Apple’s iPhone 17 press releases.
articles.body: iPhone 14 and iPhone 15 users are getting another year of free access to satellite connectivity features, according to a footnote on Apple’s newsroom posts for the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro. “The free trial will be extended for iPhone 14 and iPhone 15 users who have activated their device in a country that supports Apple’s satellite features prior to 12 a.m. PT on September 9, 2025,” Apple says. Apple originally launched its Emergency SOS service via satellite shortly after it released the iPhone 14 lineup, in November 2022, and at the time, Apple said the feature would be free for the first two years. (The feature is still free for two years after activation on iPhone 14 models and newer.) But in 2023, Apple added an additional free year for existing iPhone 14 users, meaning that the deadline to potentially start paying for the earliest adopters would be November 2025. Now, it appears that deadline has been bumped to November 2026. With iOS 18 last year, Apple expanded its satellite messaging features to let you text friends or family when you’re off the grid. Today, Apple also announced that the new Apple Watch Ultra 3 will have satellite connectivity features.

articles.title: Vizio accidentally made the best dumb TV on the market
articles.summary: The Mini LED Quantum is the cheapest quantum-dot TV you can get, but Walmart’s tracking is worrisome. Luckily you can avoid it.
articles.body: When I first started testing Vizio’s 65-inch Mini LED Quantum TV, I thought the big story was that Vizio was back and that it had a quantum-dot mini-LED TV for under $398 — the cheapest on the market. Vizio’s been pretty quiet since it was acquired by Walmart in 2024, so putting out a TV with quantum dots, which allow for higher brightness levels and more accurate color, at a budget price seemed like a strong comeback. But that’s not the big story. While those two points are intriguing, the big news about the Mini LED Quantum TV is that Vizio accidentally made the best dumb TV on the market. [Product: Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV | Walmart bought Vizio for its advertising business. Since Vizio’s ad division was responsible for all of Vizio’s profits at the time of the sale, keeping that ad revenue going is likely the priority here, and Vizio’s TV OS is the vehicle. You now need a Walmart account to use some features on a Vizio TV, and you can’t access any of the streaming apps on the Vizio Mini LED Quantum without agreeing to its activity data policy, which lets Walmart collect all your usage data. That’s annoying, but not unique. Smart TVs collect data on what you’re watching and how you watch it so they can serve targeted recommendations and ads. (Vizio was even caught doing so without consent in 2017.) --- Vizio Mini LED Quantum specs Display type: Mini LED with quantum dots HDR formats: Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10, HLG OS: Vizio OS Connections: 3 x HDMI 2.0 (one with eARC), ATSC 1.0 tuner, USB 2.0, optical audio out Audio support: Dolby Atmos, DTS: X Gaming features: 4K/60Hz, 1080p/120Hz (65-inch and up) Sizes available (inches): 43, 50, 55, 65, 75, 85 --- The potential for Walmart — much like Amazon with its Fire TVs, for that matter — is that your watch habit data can be used to target your shopping app experience. Been watching Star Wars movies and shows with the family? Maybe the next time you log in to your Walmart app you’ll get a recommendation for the Luke’s Red Five X-wing Smart Lego set. This might sound great to you, but to me, the close connection between TV OS and retailer is a bit unsettling. It’s possible to get around it, though, and to a fuller extent than on other platforms. As with any other TV, you can add an external streaming device and set the Vizio up to power on to the last used input and bypass the OS. Even with an external device, though, Vizio and Walmart are still scanning the HDMI port and collecting data on what you’re watching. But by making certain decisions during the setup process, you can keep the OS from even being active (and presumably gathering your viewing information), which I’ve never seen on other televisions. During setup, the TV asks you to sign in to, or create, a Walmart account. If you choose to skip, you’re asked if you’re sure and warned that “you will not be able to manage payments and subscriptions or link your Vizio devices.” I already manage my subscriptions through each streaming service I use, so no big loss there. After agreeing to Vizio’s terms of service and privacy policy, you’re asked to accept the activity data policy, which enables the TV’s smart features. Declining this brings up another warning screen — this one actually says “Whoops!” — informing you that “skipping this step means missing out on all your Vizio smart TV features, including apps like Netflix, YouTube, and other apps.” One last decline, and the Vizio is the dumb TV many are looking for: no OS and three HDMI ports awaiting a signal. And to make sure there’s no way Walmart is getting your info, you can always disconnect the TV from the internet entirely by forgetting your Wi-Fi settings. (You can also choose to skip connecting to Wi-Fi at the beginning of setup, which immediately switches the TV to HDMI, but you may also miss out on firmware updates.) [Image: In Calibrated mode the Vizio has a nice, bright image, although its black level isn’t that deep and the screen is reflective (you can see a reflected picture frame in the middle of the TV). And for a $400 dumb TV — or even a $400 smart TV — the 65-inch Vizio Mini LED Quantum is really good. I watched multiple World Cup matches using my OTA antenna and my normal collection of weekly shows like Last Week Tonight through my Apple TV, and they all looked pretty good. Of its picture modes, Calibrated and Calibrated Dark are the most accurate. Both lean a little toward blue, so everything has a slight cool cast. Calibrated Dark is the best for color accuracy and for a dark, light-controlled room. With SDR, it tops out at a maximum brightness of 309 nits (HDR gets up to 579 nits with small highlights). Calibrated reaches 936 nits, which is incredible for a budget TV, so its highlights and overall picture can hold up to ambient light. The screen is pretty glossy, though, so if you have lamps nearby, the reflections can be distracting, especially during dark scenes. There’s a little bit of motion blur with fast motion, which I noticed while watching the Austrian Grand Prix (especially with the cool quick-moving drone shots they introduced with that race). The Mini LED Quantum also uses an IPS panel instead of VA, so its black level isn’t as deep as a more expensive TV, and there’s some blooming visible with bright highlights in dark scenes. Most people, though, will be more than happy with the performance of the Vizio Mini LED Quantum. Even I was able to push aside my videophile expectations and relax with what I was watching. For a 65-inch TV under $400 (or up to an 85-inch for only $768), it’s easy to get past those flaws and still enjoy everyday viewing. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Of course, there are areas where Vizio’s cost-cutting is more obvious. The TV only has three HDMI 2.0 ports, when most TVs will get you four with at least one at HDMI 2.1 (though Vizio does include an ATSC 1.0 tuner). The entire back is made of a cheap-feeling plastic, there’s only one height position for the feet, and the cable management channels on the back of each foot can only accommodate a single cable each. So if you have more than one device connected to the HDMI inputs, you can’t run all the cables through the channel. The speakers, while loud, don’t sound great either (but that can be said for expensive TVs, too). If you do decide to use the Vizio OS, it’s possible to limit Walmart’s data collection by turning off Viewing Data in the TV’s privacy menu as well as unchecking personalized ads on your Vizio account page. Vizio OS is easy to navigate, if a tad sluggish sometimes. It supports all the major apps, plus AirPlay and Google Cast, and selecting different inputs is easy, both through the OS and with an input button on the small remote. After a few minutes, the TV will go into a screensaver mode, which is just one of the WatchFree+ channels that shows what looks like AI-generated scenes with music playing. But since they’re channels and not an actual screensaver, they get interrupted by ads every once in a while. It’s not the most relaxing screensaver experience. --- How I test TVs I set up each TV in my living room on my home theater credenza. I stream movies and shows through the TV’s apps and from an Apple TV, play discs on a Magnetar UDP900 MkII 4K Blu-Ray player (including the Spears & Munsil Ultra HD Benchmark disc) and movies from a Kaleidescape Strato E player, and play games on my Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5. This is done at different times of the day and under different lighting conditions, with curtains open, with lamps and overhead lights on, or with blackout curtains up to keep the room dark. While I am a certified ISF Level 3 calibrator, I do not calibrate the TVs before measurement, as the overwhelming majority of TV owners don’t bother. So it’s important to know how well the TVs perform out of the box, with minor tweaks in the menu anyone can do. For measurement, I use Portrait Displays’ Calman color calibration software, a Murideo 8K Seven pattern generator, an X-rite i1 Pro 3 spectrophotometer, Portrait Displays’ C6 HDR5000 colorimeter, a Konica Minolta LS-100 luminance meter, and Leo Bodnar 4K lag tester. --- Of course, you don’t need to worry about that if you use the Vizio Mini LED Quantum as a dumb TV. It’s not what Walmart hopes you’ll do with it, but it’s absolutely what you should. And if you want streaming apps, you can always plug in a cheap streaming device like the Fire TV Stick 4K Select for $40. If you use a connected device with the Vizio OS active, your viewing data on that device will also be shared with Walmart, according to the viewing data supplement on the privacy policy. I was concerned that down the line Vizio might find a way to force users to agree to data collection to be able to use the TV at all, but Vizio senior product manager Mike Wood told me the TV is working as intended. The hardware and picture features will always work, even if you disable the OS. “Obviously, we believe there’s a lot of benefit to using the Vizio OS and our smart features, but the choice is up to the user,” he said. That’s good news, and solidifies that the Mini LED Quantum has great performance for the price. If you’ve been looking for a big dumb TV to escape from the incessant data tracking, the Vizio Mini LED Quantum is it. Update and correction, July 7th: Vizio confirmed it is intended that the hardware (HDMI, antenna, USB, etc.) works without agreeing to any TOS/privacy/tracking policies. The last paragraph has been updated to include this information. In addition,the “Agree to continue” section below has also been corrected to indicate that accepting Viewing Data is optional. Photography by John Higgins / The Verge --- Agree to continue: Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV Every smart device now requires you to agree to a series of terms and conditions before you can use it — contracts that no one actually reads. It’s impossible for us to read and analyze every single one of these agreements. But we started counting exactly how many times you have to hit “agree” to use devices when we review them since these are agreements most people don’t read and definitely can’t negotiate. In order to manage payments and subscription or link the TV to your Walmart account, you must: * Sign in to or create a Walmart account * If you had an existing Vizio account, you must merge it with a Walmart account When creating a Walmart account, you must provide an email address and phone number, and agree to: * Walmart’s Terms of Use * Walmart’s Privacy Notice * Walmart’s Mobile Alerts Terms of Use To use the Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV fully (including Vizio OS), you must accept the following: * Vizio Terms of Service * Vizio Privacy Policy * Accept Activity Data to use streaming apps in Vizio OS Viewing Data can be accepted to allow Vizio to make content recommendations, but isn’t required and can be turned off after it was accepted, if desired. In total, you have to accept six main agreements for full functionality and can bypass three to avoid linking a Walmart account, or bypass all of them to turn the Vizio into a dumb TV when setting up the Mini LED Quantum.

articles.title: Apple Event Live Report – Will Apple Release a Folding iPhone?
articles.summary: While I won't know exactly which devices Apple will show off at the event today, its a pretty safe assumption that the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro are going to be there. There are also some strong rumors that Apple's long-expected foldable iPhone is going to make an appearance. After all, this will be the first Apple event helmed by the company's new CEO, John Ternus, so the company should have something big to mark the start of this new era.
articles.body:
Apple's annual iPhone event starts soon , at 10am PT / 1pm ET, streaming on its website and YouTube channel . The company is sure to announce its latest lineup of iPhones, Apple Watches, and maybe even some AirPods.

While I won't know exactly which devices Apple will show off at the event today, it's a pretty safe assumption that the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro will be there. Some strong rumors have been rumbling for a while that Apple's long-expected foldable iPhone is going to make an appearance. This will be the first Apple event helmed by the company's new CEO, John Ternus , so the company should have something big to mark the start of this new era.

If the foldable 'iPhone Ultra' is real, though, expect it to be very expensive. Every foldable on the market right now has a significant price jump over regular old slate phones, and Apple has never been shy about charging a premium for its new products (looking at you, Apple Vision Pro). But the price increases likely won't be limited to a foldable.

So far, Apple has avoided raising the prices on its iPhones, even though it's feeling the same RAM-flavored pressures as every other hardware manufacturer has been this year. I wouldn't be surprised if the iPhone 18 Pro costs as much as $1,399 this year, which would be $200 more expensive than last year's iPhone 17 Pro.

All of this is just speculation until Apple takes the stage and reveals which iPhones are going to be in our pockets for the next year, of course. I'll be keeping this article updated as the event goes on, so you can keep an eye on everything Apple annoounces today.

1:59pm: Apple has a new UI for the Duo, and the dock is now vertical on the side of the screen, rather than the bottom, which should make it easier to open everything with a single hand, rather than needing to grip it with both hands. When the Duo is unfolded, it looks a lot like an iPad. It looks like the OS will react naturally to whatever state the phone is in, so you should be able to prop it open in a sort of L-shape and bring up a keyboard, like a mini laptop.

1:56pm: Apple is going with a bit of a wider aspect ratio for the outer display, which is apparently "the same size as your passport". That should make the aspect ratio of the inner display a bit more usable, which seems to be Apple's goal. And, unlike the 18 Pro, the camera is underneath the display with no dynamic island. When it's unfolded, Apple claims that the iPhone Duo is the thinnest iPhone yet.

1:54pm: One more thing. Here we go. John Ternus is introducing the first Apple Foldable. It is starting off with a trailer flying over a desert, and ended on the unfolded phone with what looks like a default Mac wallpaper. And here it is, the iPhone Duo.

1:51pm: Both the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are available for preorder today, and launch on September 18. They'll cost the same as the Series 11 and Ultra 3, respectively at $399 and $799.

1:45pm: Now we're diving more into the AI capabilities of Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4. The first feature is 'audio intelligence', which will help you make sense of what you hear, which seems silly, but it can be helpful for anyone who's hard of hearing. The watch will notify you if something like a doorbell or a siren is detected. There's also a live rewind feature, where you can double tap the crown and get a transcription of what someone just said to you. That does likely mean that the Apple Watch is always listening to you, but I will admit that sometimes I zone out when someone is talking to me, so I can see the appeal here. And if you don't want the watch to listen to everything, you can turn Siri Recap off. And even if you leave it on, Apple promises that the recordings are only temporary and that Apple cannot access them.

1:42pm: The Health Sensing System will now give you a readiness report, just like the latest Pixel Watch, which will let you know when your body is ready for a rigorous workout. That way, you should be able to avoid unnecessary strain on your body. You can also order bloodwork from the Apple Watch, and the data from those tests will be uploaded to the Health app. I hope that's covered by insurance!

1:40pm: Now for the new Apple Watch 12 and Ultra 4, and of course Ternus is leading with how the Apple Watch will extend the reach of Apple Intelligence. The new watch has upgraded sensors, which make up a new "Health Sensing System." Background heart rate readings are now taken every 5 seconds, which is 60 times more frequently than the Apple Watch 11.

1:35pm: AirPods 5 is here, and it will of course have access to Siri AI, which will help you do things like live translation. And unlike the iPhone, it isn't going up in price, and will still start at $129 without noise cancelation. The new AirPods Pro is here too, with up to 5 hours of battery life with ANC enabled, and those will start at $149, which is $30 less than the last generation. Both will also be available on September 18.

1:31pm: The iPhone 18 Pro will be available for preorder on Saturday, and will be available to buy on September 18. It is more expensive than the 17 Pro, starting at $1,199, but it did say you could get it for $34.99 a month using the upgrade program. That's more expensive, but it's not as bad as I thought it'd be.

1:30pm: Apple is shrinking the dynamic island, but it doesn't seem like it's disappearing this year. I don't mind it, but I know a lot of people don't like having part of their screen cut out.

1:28pm: Apple is introducing 'Apple reference image,' which will have the camera digitally sign photos at the time of capture, so you know that it's not AI-generated. It'll also create a digital negative that can't be altered, so there's always a reference shot that you know hasn't been touched by AI.

1:23pm: The iPhone 18 Pro has a new 48mp main shooter, and it actually has a physical shutter, so you can adjust aperture beyond just software effects. This should be huge for shooting in low light, and could make the iPhone 18 Pro one of the best camera phones, but again, that's something I'll have to test when I actually get my hands on the phone. Apple is also introducting new pro controls, including white balance and lens aperture in the native camera app. Some of these photos look incredible, but professional photographers can take incredible pictures on pretty much any device, so that doesn't say much.

1:20pm: I'm excited to see how much battery life has improved. Apple claims that 5 minutes of charging will get you 6 hours of video playback. We'll see! Now we're looking at gaming on the 18 Pro, and Apple showed the phone running Monster Hunter Now, and it looked incredible. I'm going to have to check that one out.

1:18pm: Apple debuted its new vapor chamber on the 17 Pro, and it looks like there's a next-generation version of it on the 18 Pro. It has three times the surface area, which will hopefully make it a bit more effective. In my testing on the iPhone 17 Pro, the vapor chamber didn't actually impact sustained performance by much. Maybe it'll be different this year.

1:15pm: Apple Intelligence will be availble in 16 languages when the new iOS update launches later this month, and I have to admit I'm curious to see if it's actually good again. It's been a while. Now we're going to start looking at the A20 Pro, the new chipset. It has a 6-core CPU, with 2 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores. Apple claims that the 'Super cores' are desktop class, which I'll have to wait and see when I test it. The A20 Pro also has a new 7-core GPU, each with a neural accelerator, which is how Siri AI will be running natively on the phone. There's also two seperate Neural engines built into the chip, which should make the iPhone 18 Pro incredibly strong for on-device AI work.

1:12pm : It looks like Siri AI will have much more customization for the voice. I can't stop thinking of that one scene from Companion where she's trying to steal the car.

1:10pm: Apple 18 Pro seems to be built around AI, which isn't super surprising, but the company is also launching 'Siri AI'. I hope this means Apple has its own model, instead of offloading the work onto ChatGPT like previous versions of the assistant. Unrelated, it doesn't look like the dynamic island is going anywhere this year.

1:08pm: Apple is kicking off the iPhone event with another trailer, featuring the moon and then zooming in on the A20 Pro, the chip that'll be powering the iPhone 18. "This is what happens when you go to the moon, come back and ask what's next".

1:05pm: Ternus is kicking off the event talking about a new smart hub for your phone, and I'm pretty sure he's going to use this AI talk to introduce the foldable. That "big screen" he mentioned is the big clue. Either way, he's positioning the iPhone as the "ultimate personal hub". Expect a lot of Apple Intelligence here.

1:02pm: The trailer then cut to Tim Cook, introducing John Ternus as the main character. And, well, yeah I guess he is at this point.

1:00pm: Here we go! Apple spent the last 15 minutes playing music over a vague blue and pink image, which turned out to be a super-zoomed in Apple logo. Surprising! Apple kicked things off with a man burning down what looks like a circus cart. There was also an old woman who peeled off her face to reveal a younger woman! This is quite the Apple event so far.

12:45pm: The show starts in 15 minutes, and we even have music playing! It's going to be the first Apple event with John Ternus headlining, and I half-expect a Tim Cook highlight reel to kick things off. I've been watching this iPhone event every year for more than a decade now, and I wonder if the structure is just going to feel exactly the same as it has for the last few years. At least I don't have to wait long to find out.

12:30pm: We're 30 minutes out, and I still don't know how I feel about the name "Surprise and Shine." I swear Apple finds the silliest way to name its big showcases. It's even funnier, because if the big surprise is the foldable iPhone, its one we all saw coming from a mile away at this point.

12:00pm: The event starts in about an hour, and I'm still not entirely sure what is going to be there. The rumors heavily suggest the foldable is going to be there, and Mark Gurman is even calling it the 'iPhone Duo' at Bloomberg . That just makes me think of the Microsoft Surface Duo (RIP).

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Ocarina of Time remake physical preorders are $10 off at Walmart
articles.summary: Also check out discounts on the Corsair Scimitar, JBL’s touchscreen-equipped Live Beam 3 earbuds, and an Olight smart lamp.
articles.body: Nintendo announced a variety of new titles at its September livestream, but among the most talked-about is the remastered The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2. Walmart has the physical copy of the upcoming game available for preorder for just $59.88, which is $10 lower than the physical price elsewhere, and the same as the digital price. The game officially releases on November 5th, 2026, and should ship in time to reach you on launch day. [Product: The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) | The remastered title has been completely overhauled graphically, with all the shadows, details, and improved physics you would expect from a modern title. There are new quality of life improvements too, like a free camera for getting a better look at those revamped environments, and a mechanic called “Threads of Time” that helps you find your next objective. Perhaps the most shocking addition is that Link now has a dedicated jump button. In the original game, there was no way to make Link jump, outside of automatically leaping when you run off a ledge. Other deals to consider * The Corsair Scimitar RGB Elite is on sale for $49.99 at Amazon, $40 lower than the list price. This wired gaming mouse features a grid of 12 buttons on the left side, which can slide to fit different hand sizes. The extra buttons are great for MMO players in particular, though it’s also worthwhile for other games that have a lot of key bindings you’d prefer to more easily access. I have a similar gaming mouse and use it to keep all of my spells close at hand while playing World of Warcraft. * Amazon and Walmart have the JBL Live Beam 3 discounted to $129.99, an $80 discount from their list price, and close to their all-time low from Prime Day. These unique earbuds feature a 1.45-inch touchscreen on the charging case, letting you quickly check connectivity and battery level at a glance, or adjust your equalizer profile without pulling out your phone. They also have active noise cancelation, which isn’t always a given at this price point. * You can save a few bucks on the Olight Sphere C at Amazon, bringing the price down to just $12.59. This compact tabletop lamp has a magnetic base, letting it attach to many different surfaces. It also has over 20 lighting modes to choose from, including RGB options, and can run for up to 40 hours on a single charge.

articles.title: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro has a dynamic-aperture main camera
articles.summary: Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at its September 2026 “Surprise and shine” event.
articles.body: Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at its event on Wednesday. The 18 Pro and Pro Max come in deep black, silver, “glacier,” and burgundy, with color-matched back glass. They also have a new A20 Pro chip and purportedly the longest battery in an iPhone. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 for 256GB, a $100 increase over the iPhone 17 Pro, while the 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299, also for 256GB. Both models will be offered in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB configurations. Preorders begin on September 12th ahead of availability on September 18th. During Wednesday’s presentation, Apple highlighted how the new phones are well-equipped to work with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, including Siri AI’s more expressive voices. [Image: The iPhone 18 Pro’s colors: black, silver, “glacier” (blue), and burgundy. The A20 Pro has a “brand new architecture” built on 2nm technology, like Apple’s M6 chip. It has a 6 core CPU with 2 “desktop-class” super cores and 4 efficiency cores. It also has a “significantly advanced” GPU with a 7 core design that enables a “40 percent” increase in performance, according to Sribalan Santhanam, VP of Apple’s silicon engineering group. Apple has also added a second neural engine for a total of 32 NPU cores. In addition, the iPhone 18 Pro has a “next-generation vapor chamber” with three times the surface area as the one in the 17 Pro to help cool the phone. The iPhone 18 Pro has all-day battery life comparable to the iPhone 17 Pro Max, according to Rich Dinh, VP of hardware engineering. Video playback is 36 hours for the iPhone 18 Pro, and the 18 Pro Max gets 45 hours. Apple says just 15 minutes of wired charging provides 50 percent charge for the iPhone 18 Pro, and for the 18 Pro Max, five minutes of wired charging gets you seven hours of video playback. The iPhone 18 Pro also offers the “biggest camera improvement in years,” including a 48 megapixel variable-aperture main camera with 6 blades “thinner than a human hair” and a new sensor. In darker environments, the aperture opens up to let in more light, which means that night mode captures will be faster with better quality, Apple says. As for video, you can now take 4K resolution time-lapse videos in Dolby Vision HDR. [Image: Apple’s pro controls in the Photos app on an iPhone 18 Pro. Apple is also offering “pro controls” to give you more manual control over your camera, like changing shutter speed to tweak motion blur. Pro controls are available for both photos and videos. There are improvements to photographic styles, offering texture and grain control. And Apple will support Google’s SynthID content authenticity protocol, as well as a new “Apple Reference Image” standard that cryptographically signs images at capture, creating an unalterable “digital negative.” A smaller Dynamic Island on the iPhone 18 Pro line can now show three Live Activities. There are updated accessories as well, including a revised clear case. The iPhone 18 Pro line is also Apple’s first set of phones with a new C2 cellular modem, which supports mmWave 5G and “delivers meaningfully faster uploads when compared to C1X while consuming 15 percent less energy,” Apple says. [Image: Apple’s summary of what’s new in the iPhone 18 Pro. The new phones follow a major redesign introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max in 2025. That redesign dropped titanium in favor of an aluminum body, introduced a vapor chamber to help keep the phone cool, and added a camera bar (which Apple calls the “plateau”) that stretches across the back. The 17 Pro line also launched in a bold orange color that was good and well timed, a nice silver, and a great deep blue. And last fall’s iPhone refresh brought the 18-megapixel Center Stage front camera that lets you take wide selfies even when you’re holding the phone in portrait mode. Developing… see our live blog for the latest details.

articles.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max launched at ‘Surprise and Shine’ event: Price in India, specifications, features and all you need to know
articles.summary: Tech News News: Apple iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max have been launched. While the first few lines are narrated by Tim Cook, John Ternus took the centrestage for.
articles.body: Apple iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max have been launched. While the first few lines are narrated by Tim Cook, John Ternus took the centrestage for the first time as Apple’s new CEO to show off the new smartphones at the ‘Surprise and Shine’ event held at Apple Park in Cupertino, California. articles.title: The iPhone Duo is Apple’s first foldable
articles.summary: Seven years after foldable phones arrived, Apple thinks the tech is ready for an iPhone.
articles.body: Apple has announced its long-anticipated foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, which arrives more than seven years after the first Samsung Galaxy Fold hit the market. Much like Samsung’s recent Galaxy Z Fold 8, Apple says the Duo is a similar size to a passport when closed, with a 5.4-inch display, but opens to a 7.6-inch panel, the largest on any iPhone yet. Rumors have swirled about a folding iPhone since at least 2017, when it was optimistically reported that production might begin in 2020. Since then, rivals including Samsung, Google, Huawei, Oppo, Honor, and more have released myriad foldable Android phones, including larger book-style models, smaller flip phones, and more recently trifolds. The market has remained relatively small, though — just 1.6 percent of all smartphone sales in 2025. Different reports have claimed that Apple was developing variants of each of these form factors, plus larger foldable iPads, but over the last two years reporting has centered on a short, wide book-style foldable iPhone, about the size and shape of a passport when closed. That expectation is likely part of what prompted Huawei, Samsung, and Xiaomi to all release foldable phones in roughly that form factor this year, proving Apple’s industry influence remains outsize. articles.title: Apple shows off AirPods 5 with improved active noise cancellation | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The AirPods 5 support better noise cancellation, Siri AI, and offer volume controls on the stem.
articles.body:
Apple on Wednesday unveiled the latest generation of its wireless earbuds, the AirPods 5, introducing several upgrades like improved audio, stronger active noise cancellation, and expanded Siri and Apple Intelligence features.

One of the main upgrades is active noise cancellation. Apple says AirPods 5 can reduce background noise by 50% more than the previous generation, making them “the industry’s best” active noise cancellation, according to the company.

“We’re thrilled that with AirPods 5, active noise cancelation is now standard across our entire AirPods lineup. AirPods 5 are a great example of how we take the innovations from our most advanced products and bring them to the rest of the lineup, making them accessible to even more people,” CEO John Ternus said during the event.

Apple has also added volume control to the stem, a feature previously available only with the AirPods Pro. Users can swipe up or down on the stem to change the volume without reaching for their iPhone.

As with other models with the H2 chip, AirPods 5 also offer hands-free Siri and Apple Intelligence features. Users can interact with Siri without picking up their phone, whether they want to ask a question, find information, perform an action, or get directions.

The updated Siri, which Apple says will roll out in beta with iOS 27, is designed to better understand personal context. It can use information from messages, emails, photos, and other apps to provide more relevant responses and complete tasks. For example, Siri could find a restaurant mentioned in an email or play a song a friend recommended in a message.

Transparency mode in AirPods 5 has also been improved, allowing users to hear nearby voices and sounds more naturally. Adaptive Audio can automatically balance noise cancellation and Transparency mode, depending on the surrounding environment. Conversation Awareness, meanwhile, can lower the media volume when the user begins speaking.

Additionally, battery life received an upgrade, with AirPods 5 offering up to five hours of listening with active noise cancellation on a single charge. The charging case brings total listening time to up to 22 hours with active noise cancellation enabled.

AirPods 5 start at $129, while the version with a Wireless Charging Case costs $149. Pre-orders begin today, with the earbuds arriving September 18.

articles.title: Apple has a new way prove your iPhone photos aren’t AI slop | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Apple introduced Apple Reference Image to help users determine whether photos have been edited, including alterations made by AI.
articles.body:
In a world awash in AI slop, Apple wants you to trust what gets captured on its iPhones.

The company announced Wednesday during its Surprise and Shine event that it is introducing Apple Reference Image, a feature it says can prove whether an image taken with the iPhone 18 Pro is authentic.

“This is vital for photojournalists and photographers,” the company said.

When a photo is taken, the main camera sensor also captures signed sensor data which Apple’s Private Cloud Compute service then turns into an “unalterable image” viewable in the Photos app. The reference image can then be compared with other versions of the photo to determine whether any changes have been made. Apple likens the reference image to a “digital negative.”

While reference images will initially be viewable only in the Photos app, the company is making APIs available to developers so they can integrate the feature into their own apps.

Apple also said it will support the SynthID standard to help people determine whether images were created or altered with AI.

Apple Reference Image is one of several new features and upgrades to the company’s hardware and software that is focused on the camera.

The company said the iPhone 18 Pro includes its biggest camera improvement in years. One upgrade that will surely get the attention of photographers is the variable aperture on the new 48 megapixel fusion main camera. The aperture is what controls how much light enters the lens. This new main camera has a variable aperture, which means users have more control over the amount of light coming in and ultimately what the final image looks like. It should be especially helpful for those who like to take photos at night.

To achieve this, Apple said it developed a system of six laser-cut blades, each thinner than a human hair and made from a specialized polymer composite, a new rotor mechanism to control movements, and a custom-designed lens.

articles.title: Apple unveils Watch Series 12 and Watch Ultra 4 with an AI upgrade that can recap your day | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Most notably, Apple is taking aim at the growing wave of AI wearables with new "Audio Intelligence" features that let you rewind moments and remember details from daily conversations.
articles.body:
Apple on Wednesday unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 at its iPhone launch event in Cupertino. While the smartwatches aren’t getting a major hardware makeover, they are getting some significant software updates.

Most notably, Apple is taking aim at the growing wave of AI wearables with new “Audio Intelligence” features that let you rewind moments and remember details from daily conversations.

The smartwatches are launching with “Live Rewind,” a feature Apple describes as letting you go back up to 15 seconds. A double press of the Digital Crown shows the previous 15 seconds of a conversation as a text snippet. You can ask Siri about the content of that transcript, or save it to the new Siri app to revisit later.

There’s a “Siri Recap” feature that’s designed to help you remember key moments from daily conversations. It uses ambient listening to take high-level notes of your conversations, like takeaways from a team meeting or a parent-teacher conference. When Siri Recap is turned on, after a conversation, Apple Intelligence automatically generates a title and key points in the new Siri app.

A new “Sound Recognition” feature will be able to listen for sounds like sirens, alarms, doorbells, a baby crying, and more for people who are hard of hearing.

Apple says these audio intelligence features do not create or store audio recordings.

Both of the new smartwatches feature a new health-sensing system with an increased electrode surface area for better skin contact during ECG readings. For improved optical sensing, redesigned photodiodes are arranged in a ring to capture light more efficiently. There are also more power-efficient green LEDs that enable accurate heart-rate measurements throughout the day, even during motion.

The new health sensing system delivers higher-frequency continuous heart rate data, which is a key indicator of your overall health. Background heart rate readings are now taken every five seconds all day long, even while you’re on the go. That’s 60 times more frequent than before.

The smartwatches are taking a page from smart rings with new readiness scores that analyze your recent activity, vitals, and sleep each morning, distilling it all into a single score that indicates how prepared your body is to take on the day.

There’s also a new “Health Age” feature that lets users see how their key health metrics compare with their actual age, based on data from their watch, including VO2 max, sleep, and more.

The Apple Watch Series 12 starts at $399, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 costs $499.

That gives you plenty of room for some serious multitasking that just isn’t possible, or at the very least is clunky, on a smaller screen. articles.title: Apple's revamped Health app will calculate your 'health age' and readiness score | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The update uses Apple Intelligence to make better sense of your health data.
articles.body:
Alongside the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, Apple on Wednesday introduced a redesigned Apple Health app that takes advantage of Apple Intelligence to make better sense of your health data. The changes deliver a new Insights tab that includes a summary of the most timely information, plus personalized guidance, assessments, a new “readiness” score, and a computation of your “Health Age.”

The latter is a way to understand how your various health metrics compare with your actual age and uses data like your VO2 max, sleep, and more, including biomarkers from your blood.

The additions also include a new longevity tab, which uses metrics from your Apple watch and iPhone to assess your health across sleep, movement, heart health, and other factors. Your lab results can be incorporated into this guidance, and Apple announced a team-up with Quest for a 50-biomarker panel for $119, giving users quick access to data that can only come from lab tests.

With Apple Intelligence, Apple’s Health app has been improved to make sense of other health data, too, which comes into play in features like the readiness score and the Insights tab. For instance, the app could suggest that a user incorporate more intervals into their morning run to improve their cardio health. The app will also go deeper in areas like fitness and heart health as well, Apple said

The Health app also allows users to take in-depth assessments of how well their bodies are moving, which can help people who are aging or recovering from an injury. A trainer can even demonstrate certain moves for you to try as you take the assessment, which Apple claims is like having a coach right there with you.

The updated Health app rolls out later this year, starting in U.S. English.

articles.title: Apple brought ceramic back for the Series 12

articles.body: The Apple Watch Series 12 is launching with a ceramic option, making it the company’s first wearable since 2019’s Series 5 that can be configured with the pricey, scratch-resistant material. It can be configured with either pearl white or night blue ceramic finishes, and it starts at $899, going up to $949 if you purchase the 46mm size. While it started with an 18-karat rose or yellow gold case option for the first Apple Watch, the company switched to ceramic as its premium option for the Series 2, 3, and 5. Rumors had suggested Apple would only launch premium iPhones this fall, with the base model slipping to next spring. We got a look at Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone Duo, along with the next generation of AirPods and the Apple Watch. Here’s a roundup of all the biggest announcements from the event. articles.title: Apple iPhone Duo, first foldbale iPhone, launched: Price in India, specifications and features
articles.summary: Tech News News: Apple has launched the iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone, at Rs 2,99,900 in India, arriving roughly seven years after folding phones went on sale e.
articles.body: Apple has launched the iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone, at Rs 2,99,900 in India, arriving roughly seven years after folding phones went on sale elsewhere. Apple is calling it the most transformational change to the iPhone since the original, and it does break with a fair bit of iPhone convention: Face ID is gone, replaced by Touch ID in the side button, and there is no SIM tray or Action button either. It comes in star white and night sky, with pre-orders from October 16 and sales from October 23, a month after the iPhone 18 Pro.Shut, the Duo works like a normal phone. The 5.4-inch outer Super Retina XDR screen carries more than 90 per cent of the screen area of an iPhone 18 Pro. Open it and there is a 7.6-inch inner display, half again as large as the iPhone 18 Pro Max and the biggest Apple has put on an iPhone. Both screens share an aspect ratio, so content scales across them cleanly, and both run ProMotion and Always On at up to 3,000 nits. The inner panel gets a nano-texture finish that cuts glare and, more usefully, makes the crease harder to see.iPhone Duo price in India and availability: Price starts at Rs 2,99,900 and pre-orders open on October 16The Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900 and runs to four storage tiers. Pre-orders open at 5:30 pm IST on Friday, October 16, and the phone reaches Apple's own store and select partner stores on Friday, October 23.StoragePrice (India)256GBRs 2,99,900512GBRs 3,24,9001TBRs 3,74,9002TBRs 4,49,900Apple is running the usual launch offers alongside. Trade-in credit ranges from Rs 4,500 to Rs 81,500 depending on what you hand over, there is No Cost EMI of up to six months, and instant cashback of up to Rs 7,000 on American Express, Axis Bank and ICICI Bank cards. The box holds the phone and a USB-C cable, with no adapter and no earphones. Two first-party cases are being sold separately: the Duo Folio with a retractable kickstand at Rs 14,900 and a lighter two-part case at Rs 8,900, both of which work with MagSafe and Qi2. One thing to settle before ordering is connectivity, because the Duo is eSIM-only worldwide and has no tray at all, though Airtel, Jio and Vi all support eSIM in India.It is worth holding that starting price against the rest of the range. The iPhone 18 Pro begins at Rs 1,64,900 and the iPhone 18 Pro Max above it, which puts the Duo at close to twice the cost of a Pro for a phone that carries the same chip and a smaller camera system. What the money buys is the folding screen and the software built for it, not better photography. AppleCare+ is offered as usual, and given that this is a first-generation folding device with a hinge that has to survive years of opening and closing, it is a more relevant question here than on a regular iPhone.iPhone Duo specifications: A20 Pro chip, dual batteries and a 48MP Dual Fusion cameraThe inner display is built from ten ultra-thin layers with wide-angle OLEDs, and the FaceTime camera sits under the panel so nothing interrupts the surface. Durability is where Apple has done its longest engineering pitch. Under the cover layer is a custom polymer the company says is up to 40 per cent stiffer than the industry norm, with high-strength glass above and below the folding panel and adhesives that let the layers slide against each other like pages, so the screen does not absorb the bend stress. A titanium plate runs along the base. The hinge alone uses more than a hundred parts. The frame and hinge cover are grade 5 titanium, the front carries Ceramic Shield 2 with three times the scratch resistance of the last generation, and the phone is rated IP68.Inside is the same A20 Pro as the iPhone 18 Pro, built on a 2nm process, with a 6-core CPU that is 20 per cent quicker than the A19 Pro, a 7-core GPU up 40 per cent, a dual 16-core Neural Engine and 50 per cent more memory bandwidth. A new display engine drives both screens at once. Apple claims up to 35 per cent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro, helped by a vapour chamber bonded to the chip package. A battery sits on each side and the two behave as one, giving 31 hours of video on the inner display, 44 hours on the outer, and 24 hours of typical use when both get equal work. Charging reaches 50 per cent in about 20 minutes over cable, or around 30 minutes on MagSafe. The N1 chip handles Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread, and Apple's own C2 modem does cellular.Apple has also made a point of the phone holding whatever position you leave it in. It can be used partly folded, stood in a tent shape on its edges, or propped like a small laptop, and iOS reads the angle from sensors in each half and reorients accordingly. Speakers sit at the top and bottom with tuning that accounts for how far apart they end up in each pose. There is no Action button on the Duo, a small loss for anyone who has got used to it on recent iPhones, though Camera Control survives and now launches the new Siri mode in the camera app.The camera is the one place where the Duo is not the flagship. It uses a 48MP Dual Fusion system, a Fusion Main with sensor-shift stabilisation and a 2x optical-quality crop plus the same 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide as the iPhone 18 Pro. There is no dedicated telephoto, no variable aperture and no Pro controls, all of which stay exclusive to the Pro models, and Apple Reference Image is missing too. What the Duo gets instead are tricks the shape allows. Smart Take fires the shutter when it sees everyone posed, Duo Preview puts a live preview on the outer screen so your subject can frame themselves, Kid Cue plays animations to pull a child's eyes to the lens, and Duo FaceTime lets someone beside you join a call on the outer display. Video goes up to 4K at 120 fps in Dolby Vision, and Photographic Styles 3 adds texture and grain controls. The front camera is a 12MP Center Stage unit, with the under-display FaceTime camera shooting 1080p.iPhone Duo software: iOS 27 rebuilt around two screens, with Siri AI in betaThe Duo ships with iOS 27.1, and the interface has been reworked rather than stretched. Lock Screen controls, the dock and app navigation shift to the side to free up vertical space, the Dynamic Island is redesigned to run vertically along the edge of either display, and opening the phone brings up two Home Screen pages with a scrolling Today View on the left. Content reorients as the phone folds, turns or flips over.The multitasking is the part that will decide whether the extra screen earns its money. Split View puts two apps side by side on an iPhone for the first time, you can open two windows of the same app, and app pairs can be saved and reopened together. StandBy now works on either display even when the phone is not charging, turning it into a clock, photo frame or widget panel in tent mode. Netflix, Zoom and Slack have already adapted their apps, and Apple Pencil support arrives later this year on both screens.Beyond the assistant, Apple Intelligence brings the photo tools that arrived with iOS 27 across the range: Spatial Reframing to recompose a shot after the fact, Extend to widen it, and a Clean Up tool that can now remove larger objects. Safari can watch a page and alert you when a price drops or something restocks, and Call Context surfaces a booking code from your mail when you ring an airline. Some of these lean on Apple's servers and carry daily usage limits. Anyone moving over from Android can use the Move to iOS app to bring across photos, messages, contacts and calendars.Siri AI, the rebuilt assistant Apple showed at WWDC, is rolling out in beta with iOS 27 from Monday, September 14, in English first, with more languages in October. It pulls personal context from messages, mail and photos, takes actions inside apps and answers general questions, and Apple is pitching the large inner screen as the best place to hold that conversation.iPhone Duo specifications at a glanceSpecificationiPhone DuoInner display7.6-inch Super Retina XDR folding, nano-texture, ProMotion, Always On, 3,000 nitsOuter display5.4-inch Super Retina XDR, same aspect ratio, ProMotion, Always OnChipA20 Pro, 2nm, 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU, dual 16-core Neural EngineRear camera48MP Fusion Main with sensor-shift OIS, 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide, 2x optical-quality zoomFront camera12MP Center Stage on outer display, under-display FaceTime camera insideVideo4K at up to 120 fps in Dolby Vision, 4K time-lapse, Photographic Styles 3BatteryDual battery, 31 hours video on inner display, 44 hours on outer, 24 hours typical useCharging50 per cent in about 20 minutes wired, about 30 minutes on MagSafeSecurityTouch ID in the side button, no Face IDBuildGrade 5 titanium frame and hinge cover, Ceramic Shield 2 front, IP68ConnectivityeSIM only, C2 modem, N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and ThreadSoftwareiOS 27.1 with Split View, StandBy, Siri AI in beta, Apple Pencil support later this yearStorage256GB, 512GB, 1TB, 2TBColoursStar white, night skyPrice in IndiaFrom Rs 2,99,900Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Hands-on with the foldable iPhone Duo
articles.summary: We’ve tried the first foldable iPhone at Apple’s launch event.
articles.body: The first foldable iPhone is finally here, and following its announcement, we got the chance to try the phone for ourselves. We’ve long been told that Apple would make a foldable iPhone once the tech was good enough — has it been worth the wait? [Image: It definitely feels like something different. The inner screen has a decidedly matte finish that handled even some glare from the windows above the hands-on area well. The folding mechanism is smooth, and even IP68 rated, and the crease is almost impossible to find with my finger. The 5.4-inch outer screen looks petite by modern slab phone standards. [Media: The real show happens when you open and close the phone — rather than just switching one screen off and lighting the other one up, there’s a gradual transition that happens, and it looks as if the contents of the screen come into focus as it moves toward its final position. It’s a pretty nice touch. I also saw the phone positioned in laptop mode with Netflix on the inner screen, displaying controls on the bottom half before fading them away. There’s also the usual tricks in tent mode, where you’ll get StandBy even if you don’t have the phone plugged in. I’m very curious to see what that does to battery life. Rumors that a foldable iPhone was in the works have been circulating since at least 2017, with Samsung releasing its first foldable two years after that. Since then, almost every Android manufacturer has entered the market, including Google, Motorola, Huawei, Xiaomi, Oppo, and more. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Over the last decade, Apple has been variously reported to be developing traditional book-style folding iPhones, smaller flip phone variants, and even larger foldable iPads, before it eventually settled on its final form factor. While early rumors suggested it would be like having two iPhone Airs side by side, the 1.4:1 aspect ratio is squatter, closer to a passport book when closed. That makes the 7.6-inch internal screen wider and better suited for watching videos in landscape than other foldables, but great for reading long scrolling pages or multitasking in portrait. [Image: The dual main camera setup shoots 48-megapixel photos and includes a 2x optical zoom. It’s largely the same as the iPhone 18 Pro but lacks the variable aperture.

articles.summary: The iPhone 18 Pro launches on September 18th starting at $1,199. We’ve compared the new model’s specs with previous Pro models.
articles.body: Apple’s release cadence for the latest iPhones is unusual. It’ll start with the 18 Pro models, then with the foldable iPhone Duo releasing in October for $1,999. It hasn’t confirmed when its base iPhone 18 model will launch. So this post is focused just on the new the 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max. Both phones are launching on September 18th, with preorders opening Saturday, September 12th. The 6.3-inch iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199, which is $100 more than last year’s phone. The 6.9-inch iPhone 18 Pro Max goes up to $1,299, another $100 jump. With the iPhone 18 Pro being Apple’s 2026 flagship phone, it makes sense to compare it to its two predecessors to see how things have evolved. The biggest differences between the two sizes of this year’s Pro phone are the same as always: the physical dimensions, the battery size, and the size and resolution of the screen. The specs are otherwise identical. But compared to previous Pros, the most meaningful updates come with the cameras, performance, and speed for chewing through AI-related tasks. By holding off on unveiling its base iPhone 18 until a later date, Apple is making deciding on a new phone this fall a little easier — that is, if you’re someone who typically buys the pricey Pro variant. articles.title: Hands-on with the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4
articles.summary: ﻿Apple’s latest watches come with some new Siri AI features and the return of ceramic cases.
articles.body: After Apple wrapped up its “Surprise and shine” event today, we were able to get a look at the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. [Image: Ceramic is back, baby. Both of the new watches launch September 18th, with preorders available starting today. The Apple Watch Series 12 once again starts at $399 for the aluminum case option in space gray, black, light gold, and dark bronze aluminum. The natural or radiant gold titanium version costs $699, and the night blue or pearl white ceramic costs $899. Apple says this year’s watch offers up to 24 hours of “everyday” battery life, and now offers up to 10 hours of battery during outdoor workouts and supports faster charging with up to 12 hours’ worth recharged in just 15 minutes. The ceramic Series 12 sure does look and feel nice in person. The night blue version is very fetching, but the stark pearl white is also très chic on the wrist. The new dark bronze did look a lot darker in person, however. Like how the dark green Series 7 looked a bit less green and more blackish green, there’s a similar vibe with the bronze. [Image: See what I mean about the bronze color? The Series 12 runs on a new S11 chip that powers a few new Audio Intelligence Siri AI features, including Sound Recognition, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It also got some health upgrades, including new optical and electrical heart sensors with support for continuous background heart rate sensing that takes readings every five seconds. There’s also a new Health Age feature that compares your health metrics to your chronological age, and a Readiness feature that gives you a score for how to handle the day ahead based on your recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score. The Readiness feature will be limited to the Series 12 and Ultra 4, however, because it requires the new heart rate sensor array. [Image: You can see the difference between the sensor array on the Ultra 4 and the Ultra 3 (right). Speaking of the array, this is the first major update on this front in a while. You can definitely see the difference side by side. Notably, the Apple reps on hand pointed out that the new Series 12 and Ultra 4 have a “32-petal design,” whereas the older watches had a two-petal design. This refers to the spoke-like lines coming out of the electrode. It should theoretically enable much more accurate readings. You can also see that the optical sensors themselves are situated much closer together. This is to help minimize light leakage. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 also includes the new S11 chip and Audio Intelligence features. It starts at $799 and comes in natural and black titanium, along with a premium Apple Watch Hermès version. Apple says the Ultra 4 offers up to 50 hours of battery life. [Image: [Image: [Image:

articles.title: Apple Announces Foldable iPhone Duo
articles.summary: After years of it being rumored, Apple has finally revealed a foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo at the company's "Surprise and Shine" September event. Here's all the camera details, performance specs, and UI improvements Apple is packing into its newest device.
articles.body:
After years of it being rumored, Apple has finally revealed a foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, at the company's "Surprise and Shine" September event .

Unlike other foldables, such as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, the iPhone has the same aspect ratio in both folded and unfolded forms. When folded, the Duo has a 5.4-inch display – about the side of a passport – and unfolds to 7.6 inches. Both of these displays have a 1.4:1 aspect ratio – for context, that's in-between a 4:3 aspect ratio (equal to 1.34:1) and 16:9 (equal to 1.7:1).

Apple says it went with this format in order to maximize the usage of the larger, unfolded display. Most other foldables have a mostly-square shape when unfolded, which Apple points out wastes space to letterbox black bars when viewing traditional 16:9 content. The screen uses wide-angle OLEDs, and has a 3,000-nit peak brightness.

As with practically every foldable announcement in history, Apple says that it worked hard on eliminating the crease, and while we'll have to wait until we get our hands on it to say for sure, it seems like the company was successful. The iPhone Duo uses what Apple is calling a "nano-texture display" to maintain optimal screen-feel while doing what it needs to do in order to not have a visable crease. When unfolded, Apple says the Duo is the thinnest iPhone ever.

Powering this foldable iPhone is Apple's new A20 Pro chipset, the same found in the iPhone 18 Pro . With other foldables with flagship chipsets, you typically see slightly slower performance, especially in sustained workloads, because the phone ironically has less space to cool the chip. The iPhone Duo, meanwhile, utilizes a vapor chamber cooling system, but we'll have to wait for hands-on testing before passing judgement on how well it keeps things cool. More importantly, the A20 Pro chip is going to power both the internal and external display simultaneously, which means that there'll be essentially zero delay when swapping between screens.

The UI has been completely redesigned for the iPhone Duo, with primary controls and the dynamic island moved to the side of the screen. This should make things easier to access and activate when holding the phone in one hand. Plus, that aspect ratio mentioned above will give you more space to watch videos and play games, meaning the iPhone Duo has a shot at becoming the best foldable for gaming .

Apple showed off a variety of interesting use cases for the iPhone Duo. Standby mode works well here, as you can prop up a semi-folded Duo on your nightstand to serve as a bedside clock and alarm.

The camera system also gets some neat tricks. You can have the outer display preview the image, so your subject can see how your framing looks before the photo is taken – surely a boon for hapless Instagram partners everywhere. There's also a cool feature that lets you display a captivating animation, such as a clip of Snoopy dancing, in order to draw the attention of a child towards the camera. Meanwhile, Duo Facetime uses both the internal and external screens and cameras to let people on both sides of the device join a FaceTime call instead of having to crowd around a small screen and camera.

As for the camera itself, the main sensor is the same 48MP shooter as the iPhone 18 Pro, though it lacks the physical aperture shutter of that phone. Meanwhile, the internal camera is 12MP and sits under the display, remaining hidden until you need it.

Battery life is always a challenge on foldables, but Apple claims the iPhone Duo will be capable of "all-day" usage. That's an impressive claim, and one we'll surely be testing when we go hands-on with the device.

The iPhone Duo will be available in Night Sky (dark grey) and Star White colorways, and starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage, which is $100 less than the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. Preorders start on October 16, with the phone hitting store shelves on October 23.

For more on Apple's latest hardware, including the new iPhone 18 Pro , check out our roundup of everything announced at the September Apple event .

articles.title: The hinge for Apple's new foldable phone was built with AI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Apple says it used AI and 3D printing in the manufacturing process for its long-awaited foldable phone.
articles.body:
Apple’s long-awaited foldable phone, the Duo, contains a number of surprises, including a critical hinge that was designed and built with the help of AI and 3D printing.

The new phone represents Apple’s first entry into the foldable phone genre — a category of devices that has seen significant consumer enthusiasm, but whose form factors haven’t always lived up to that enthusiasm. As you might expect from a product that, by design, undergoes twice as much wear as a traditional device, most foldables suffer significant degradation and don’t have the durability of other smartphones.

Apple claims that it has integrated innovative protections into the Duo’s design to keep the phone from falling prey to the typical wear and tear associated with foldables. That includes the hinge, according to Johny Srouji, the company’s chief hardware officer.

“During manufacturing, we use AI algorithms to precisely match each individual hinge with its best-fit housing to ensure perfect alignment, and a confocal laser progressively scans the topology of every single unit, and 3D prints up to 25 micro layers of a custom photopolymer to eliminate residual waviness,” Srouji said during Apple’s Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday.

Srouji also shared that Apple gave the foldable phone “a custom nano-texture finish that significantly reduces glare and reflections” as well as a multi-layer lamination strategy designed to increase the device’s durability. Of course, it remains to be seen whether those protections will be enough to keep the Duo in peak physical condition in the long run.

articles.title: Apple’s new iPhone camera mode promises to prove your photo isn’t AI
articles.summary: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro lineup will come with a new “Reference Image” feature that claims to prove a photo isn’t made with AI.
articles.body: Apple is launching a new way to prove that the picture you took isn’t manipulated by AI. A new feature, called “Reference Image,” will arrive with the iPhone 18 Pro lineup later this month and is supposed to use the device’s new camera sensor to “sign every pixel it sees.” The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will only authenticate photos when placed into Reference mode. Once the camera captures signed sensor data, Apple says its Private Cloud Compute will develop it “into an unalterable reference image” that can be viewed in the Photos app. You’ll be able to compare the reference image with other versions of the photo to see if any edits were made. [Image: You can compare the Reference Image to other versions of the photo. As AI-generated images and videos become more realistic, several new standards have emerged to label images not created by a human, such as SynthID, C2PA, and Meta’s Content Seal. Apple is putting a twist on these methods by building authentication directly into its hardware. Apple is letting developers access a Reference Image API across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, which could eventually allow users to inspect these digitally signed photos in third-party apps. The company says the iPhone 18 Pro lineup won’t come with its Reference Image feature at launch in the European Union, but it says users in the region will still be able to “develop and view” them in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.

articles.title: The foldable iPhone Duo is here: Plus everything Apple announced at its fall iPhone event
articles.summary: Here's everything Apple announced today at the "Surprise and shine" fall iPhone event.
articles.body:
If you buy something through a link in this article, we may earn commission.

It's safe to say that Apple's annual fall event is one of the most anticipated happenings in the tech world. Usually, Tim Cook and his cohorts in Cupertino unveil a few new iPhones, an Apple Watch or two and perhaps some AirPods. That's exciting enough in its own right, but this year is different. For one, Tim Cook stepped down as CEO and his replacement, John Ternus, took over just nine days ago, making today the new leader's first launch event.

But what really set the "Surprise and Shine" event apart from prior years in recent memory is the announcement of the iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable phone . Apple said nothing official before the keynote today, so everyone in the tech world — us included — had to wait until the device was revealed on-stage. The new device is definitely the headliner, but Apple also revealed two new phones (the iPhone 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max ) as well as new AirPods and two new wearables (the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and the Apple Watch Series 12 ). Here's everything Apple announced during today's iPhone keynote in California.

If Apple didn't end up announcing a foldable iPhone, the tech world would have lost its collective mind. Thankfully, Apple did not disappoint and the iPhone Duo is here. As expected, it has a "passport" design that creates a 5.4-inch screen when folded and a 6.7-inch iPad-mini-like screen when lying flat. People I talked to said Apple went this route because a wider internal screen is better for consuming media. Plus the familiar iPad vibe is, well, familiar to the Apple customer.

Apple said their model will re-design the experience of using a foldable phone. For one, it's the largest display ever on an iPhone. The body is made from aero-grade titanium and has a unique hinge made from more than 100 components and supports the center of the screen when open to help it lie flat. Apple says it's the thinnest iPhone ever when it's opened.

The 7.6-inch internal display is 80% larger than that of the iPhone 18 Pro (and a touch smaller than the iPad mini display which comes in at 8.3-inches). Apple says the 5.4-inch outer display will give nearly 90% of the screen real estate that you get with the iPhone 18 Pro. That screen comes with a scratch-resistant coating and a custom polymer cover layer for the inner screen that's up to 40% stiffer than materials used on other foldables.

The user interface won't feel exactly the same as either an iPhone or iPad, thanks to a completely redesigned operating system. It'll even support the USB-C Apple Pencil. From the use-case examples Apple shared, it seems the design really utilizes the folding format. The outer screen gives you selfie previews or can show animations to your kids when you're trying to get them to smile for the camera. Apple also included the beloved "flex mode" which lets you stand the phone in the half-folded position for viewing the screen or taking hands-free group shots. Many people will certainly enjoy the Duo FaceTime mode that lets the person you're talking to see both you and what you're looking at.

The foldable will start at $1,999 for 256GB of storage and it'll be available for pre-order starting October 16. It should hit shelves and start shipping out October 23.

The first devices (though not the headliners) announced today, were the two new Pro model iPhones. After being treated to a slew of movie opening shots (all filmed on iPhones, we were told) Tim Cook metaphorically passed the reigns to John Ternus. The new CEO introduced himself and let us know his thoughts on Apple devices, AI and Apple apps. Ternus described the "Intelligent Personal Hub," teasing things like great cameras, big screens, all-day batteries and "something that's always with you." He was, of course, describing an iPhone and talked about AI as well as data security.

We also got an overview of the new Siri AI, which we've tested already , as well as new camera tools from iOS 27. Then, finally, the iPhone Pro models were shown off for the first time.

Both models run on the A20 Pro chip that sets "a new bar for mobile computing," with desktop-class super cores and enable the "fastest processing speeds on any smartphone". To mitigate heat, a new thermal management offers 3X the surface area than last year and the new vapor chamber includes "industry first" copper nano layer to dissipate heat. All of this, Apple says, adds up to 40% improved heat performance.

The battery on the 18 Pro should last as long at last year's iPhone 17 Pro Max (36 hours) and the 18 Pro Max will get a whopping 45-hour lifespan from a charge.

The new camera includes aperture control on the 48MP main fusion camera using physical shutters that are thinner than a human hair. In short, it lets in more light in dark scenes and can handle better depth-of-focus shots. Apple also went over a slew of cinematic features (no doubt enabling those movie clips we saw at the beginning of the show) as well as the creation of a a "Reference Photo" (that can't be altered) to act as a digital negative — an important feature in our AI unreality.

Both Pro models will open for pre-orders on September 12. The Pro model starts at $1,199 and the Pro Max starts at $1,299. The phones will hit shelves on September 18. Apple is offering trade in values of up to $1,200 with a series 14 trade-in or newer.

With the launch of the AirPods 5 , active noise cancellation is now available for all Apple wireless earbuds. This is the model with the open ear fit (compared to the AirPods Pro that insert into your ear canal). The new model has been redesigned to fit more ears. And immersive audio should now be, well, more immersive. Noise reduction is up to 50% higher than the AirPods 4 and Apple says the transparency mode will sound more natural too. Thanks to integration with Siri AI, the AirPods 5 will support live translation. Sweat and dust resistance was also increased.

AirPods 5 will start at $129 (which was the same starting price as the non-ANC AirPods 4). There's also a model with longer battery life and a wireless charging case that'll sell for$149. Pre-orders are open today and the buds will be widely available September 18.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4

Last year, Apple hit us with three new wearables: the flagship Series 11 as well as the budget SE 3 and premium Ultra 3. This year, it looks like we get a new flagship and an Ultra (the SE doesn't typically get yearly refreshes). Both watches come with redesigned sensor arrays that support something Apple is calling the Health Sensing System. The array should have better skin contact as well as larger LEDs to support more accurate heart-rate data. Apple said they tested these new sensors against other wearables, and found, of course, that they beat all competitors. One can imagine, had that not been the case, the study would have gone unmentioned.

All data gathered by the watch goes into the Health app, which will now be powered by Apple Intelligence, sort of like what Google did . The entire Health app has been redesigned to include AI assistance that can offerer suggestions. Wearing the watch will also enable a "Health Age" as well as a "Longevity" score within the Health app. Just in case you want to see how your fitness and health efforts affect your theoretical lifespan.

The watch is also coming for those AI wearables you may have heard about. Both watches will enable "audio intelligence" that uses the on-board microphone to listen to what's going on around you. The feature will alert the hard of hearing to things like sirens and every one can use "live rewind" to play back the past 15 seconds of what was just said. Another feature, Siri Recap, can take notes when enabled, and can record and transcribe your conversations.

Both watches use the S11 chip, which have a new audio processing module to handle the above features, as well as a faster CPU and GPU derived from the phone's A20 Pro.

The glass on the Series 12 is 60% tougher and the battery life will last the same 24 hours as the Series 11, but the recharge time has dropped to 15 minutes to get 12 hours of battery life. New colors for the flagship include grey, black, gold and a new dark bronze. There's also a new ceramic case material available that comes in pearl white and night blue.

The Ultra 4 gets two days of battery life, including 18 hours of workout tracking. It comes in black and natural titanium. The starting price is $399 for the Apple Series 12 GPS model. The Ultra 4 will start at $799. Pre-orders open today and the watches will be available September 18.
